name: ADC082S101CIMMX_NOPB
title: ADC082S101: two-input 8-bit SAR ADC, 500 ksps to 1 Msps, serial interface, VSSOP-8
summary: An 8-bit successive-approximation converter with a two-way input multiplexer and its own track-and-hold, specified across the whole span from 500 ksps to 1 Msps. It runs from one supply of 2.7 V to 5.25 V, and that supply is also the reference, so the input span is 0 V to VA. A four-wire SPI/QSPI/MICROWIRE-style port (CS, SCLK, DIN, DOUT) starts each conversion, picks the next channel and shifts the result out MSB first in straight binary. Raising CS powers the part down to a fraction of a microwatt. One package: 8-lead VSSOP (DGK), -40 °C to +85 °C.
key_figures: 500 ksps to 1 Msps (fSCLK 8 MHz to 16 MHz, 16 clocks per conversion)

pins.name: CS
pins.function: Chip select, active low. A falling edge starts a conversion; conversions repeat for as long as it stays low. High puts DOUT in high impedance and powers the part down.

pins.name: VA
pins.function: Supply, +2.7 V to +5.25 V, and the conversion reference. Bypass to GND with 1 µF plus 0.1 µF monolithic, both within 1 cm of the pin, from a quiet source.

pins.name: IN1
pins.function: Analog input 1, 0 V to VA. The first conversion after power-up reads this input.

pins.name: DIN
pins.function: Serial data in. Loads the control register on SCLK rising edges.

pins.name: DOUT
pins.function: Serial data out. Result bits change on SCLK falling edges, MSB first; high impedance while CS is high.

pins.name: SCLK
pins.function: Serial clock. Times both the conversion and the data transfer.

circuits.title: Typical application
circuits.description: An LP2950 low-dropout regulator takes a 5 V rail down to a dedicated supply for VA, with 1 µF and 0.1 µF on its input and the same pair on its output beside the converter. Because VA is the reference, a clean separate regulator keeps supply noise out of the result; a precision reference could feed VA instead, the supply current being small. IN1 and IN2 are the two analog inputs. SCLK, CS and DIN come from a microprocessor or DSP, and DOUT returns to it.

operation.text: A successive-approximation converter built on a charge-redistribution DAC. In track mode a switch joins the sampling capacitor to the channel the multiplexer has chosen while a second switch balances the comparator. In hold mode the capacitor is switched to ground, keeping its charge, and the control logic steps charge in from the DAC until the comparator balances; the DAC code at that point is the result. The part tracks during SCLK cycles 1 to 3 counted from the CS falling edge, and holds and converts during cycles 4 to 16.

A frame runs from the falling edge of CS to its rising edge and holds a whole multiple of 16 rising SCLK edges; each 16 clocks is one conversion. DOUT is active only while CS is low. The result leaves DOUT MSB first from the 5th clock, after four leading zeros, followed by four trailing zeros. With several conversions in one frame, the part goes back to tracking on the SCLK falling edge after rising edge N×16 and to hold/convert on falling edge N×16+4.

On the first 8 SCLK rising edges after CS falls, DIN loads the control register, and that word chooses the input for the next conversion, not the current one. The first conversion after power-up converts IN1. ADD1 must be 0; with it set the output is undefined.

SCLK is gated off inside the part while CS is high. If SCLK idles low, the CS falling edge itself acts as the first SCLK falling edge and tracking starts there. If SCLK idles high, tracking starts on the first SCLK falling edge after CS falls. CS and SCLK falling inside the tCSU/tCLH window can shift the DIN clocking by one cycle, so those minimum times should be met.
No start-up delay or dummy conversion is needed: the first conversion after power is applied is a full one.
Straight binary output. One LSB is VA/256; code transitions fall halfway between whole LSB values, the first at VA/512, the top one (to 1111 1111) at VA − 1.5 LSB.

The supply is the reference, so noise on VA appears in the result. A dedicated linear regulator for VA is recommended, or enough decoupling to isolate it from other circuits; with its low current, VA may also be fed from a precision reference. Bypass VA with 1 µF and 0.1 µF placed close to the pin.

Each input has ESD diodes to VA and GND. Inputs must stay between GND − 300 mV and VA + 300 mV, beyond which the diodes conduct and the part may misbehave; the diodes are not meant as signal clamps. The input model is about 3 pF of pin capacitance, then about 500 Ω of multiplexer and switch resistance into the 30 pF sampling capacitor, which is connected while tracking and open during conversion. A low-impedance source avoids distortion from charging the sampling capacitor, which matters most for AC signals; a low-pass or band-pass filter ahead of the input cuts noise and harmonics.
DOUT swings no higher than VA. SCLK, CS and DIN do not latch up and may be driven before VA is applied, though doing so is not recommended.

CS low is full power and CS high is full power-down. The part also drops into power-down on its own between the 16th SCLK falling edge of one conversion and the first falling edge of the next. Conversions repeat for as long as CS is held low, 16 SCLK cycles each. For lower power at a given throughput, run SCLK at 16 MHz and convert less often, leaving the part in shutdown between conversions.

Current to charge the DOUT load comes from VA, and discharging it dumps current into the resistive substrate; both couple noise into the conversion and degrade SNR and SINAD as load capacitance grows. Keep the DOUT load small; above 50 pF, put 100 Ω in series with DOUT close to the pin.
ESD protection is limited; store with leads shorted or in conductive foam.
